actions.justification: MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: measure serum lactate immediately to stratify severity (lactate >=4 mmol/L indicates high mortality risk and triggers aggressive fluid resuscitation). Must be done within 60 minutes.
MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: obtain blood cultures BEFORE administering antibiotics to identify causative organism and guide de-escalation. This must precede antibiotic administration.

MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: administer empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately after blood cultures are drawn. Strong recommendation to give within 1 hour of septic shock recognition. Patient has CKD stage 4 and diabetes — dose-adjust renally cleared agents accordingly.

MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: administer 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid for hypotension (BP 88/52, MAP 64). Patient is in septic shock and requires immediate fluid resuscitation despite CKD stage 4; this is the highest priority remaining mandatory action.

Patient has altered mental status, decreased urine output, and CKD stage 4 — evaluate for multi-organ dysfunction (renal, hepatic, coagulation, neurologic) to guide resuscitation targets and escalation decisions.
BMP is critical in this patient with CKD stage 4, diabetes, and suspected septic shock to assess renal function (creatinine, BUN), electrolytes, glucose, and guide fluid and vasopressor management.

Patient remains in septic shock (MAP 64, HR 110, SpO2 93%). Serial vital sign assessment is critical to monitor response to fluids and antibiotics already administered, and to guide vasopressor initiation if MAP falls below 65 mmHg.

Per SSC guidelines, vasopressors should be applied if patient remains hypotensive during or after fluid resuscitation to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg. BP is 88/52 (MAP 64) and 30 mL/kg crystalloid has been given; norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor for septic shock.
Identifying the source of infection (urinary given decreased urine output, pulmonary given SpO2 93%, or other) is essential to guide antibiotic targeting and determine if source control is needed.

Initial lactate was 4.0 mmol/L (≥4 mmol/L threshold). SSC guidelines mandate serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation and assess response to treatment. Remeasuring is essential to evaluate whether interventions are improving tissue perfusion.

Patient is 45 minutes into resuscitation with fluids and vasopressors initiated. Reassessment of perfusion (MAP, mental status, urine output) is critical to determine adequacy of resuscitation and guide next steps per SSC guidelines.
CBC is indicated to evaluate for leukocytosis/leukopenia (infection severity), thrombocytopenia (DIC risk), and anemia — all relevant in this septic shock patient with CKD stage 4 and diabetes.

Patient on vasopressor (norepinephrine) with ongoing hemodynamic instability (MAP 64, BP 88/52). Arterial line provides continuous blood pressure monitoring essential for vasopressor titration and frequent blood draws.
Central venous access needed for reliable vasopressor administration, CVP monitoring, and potential ScvO2 measurement to guide resuscitation in septic shock.
Patient with septic shock and elevated lactate 4.0 is at risk for DIC. Coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) are indicated to assess for coagulopathy as part of organ dysfunction evaluation.

Procalcitonin is a useful biomarker to confirm bacterial infection, guide antibiotic stewardship, and monitor treatment response in septic shock. Patient has elevated lactate (4.0), ongoing hemodynamic instability, and all mandatory Hour-1 bundle elements are complete.

Chest X-ray is indicated to identify a pulmonary source of infection (pneumonia, effusion) given fever, altered mental status, and SpO2 of 93%. Identifying the infection source guides targeted therapy.

Patient has CKD stage 4 requiring careful fluid management, but MAP is borderline at 64 mmHg and lactate remains elevated at 4.0. Additional judicious crystalloid may support resuscitation alongside norepinephrine, guided by response monitoring.

Patient remains in septic shock with MAP 64 mmHg (borderline) and HR 110 despite norepinephrine already initiated. Vasopressin can be added as a second vasopressor per SSC guidelines to augment MAP, reduce norepinephrine requirements, and help achieve MAP ≥65 mmHg target. This is the only remaining available action and is clinically appropriate given persistent hemodynamic instability.

MANDATORY action: Patient remains hypotensive (MAP 64, BP 88/52) and tachycardic (HR 110) despite prior fluid resuscitation. SSC guidelines mandate vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg in septic shock. This must be completed immediately.

Patient has septic shock with lactate 4.0, hypotension requiring vasopressors, CKD stage 4, altered mental status, and SpO2 93%. ICU-level care is required for continuous monitoring, vasopressor titration, and organ support.
